(20 June 2015) | longest wins = [[Association Sportive Tanda|Tanda]] (6) | longest unbeaten = [[Sporting Club de Gagnoa|Sporting Gagnoa]] (15) | longest winless = Bouaké (8) | longest losses = [[AS Denguélé|Denguélé]] (4) | matches = 182 | total goals = 307 | prevseason = [[2013–14 Ligue 1 (Ivory Coast)|2013–14]] | nextseason = [[2015–16 Ligue 1 (Ivory Coast)|2015–16]] }} The '''2014–15 [[Ligue 1 (Ivory Coast)|Ligue 1]]''' is the 56th season of top-tier football in [[Ivory Coast|Côte d'Ivoire]]. The season began on 28 November 2014. [[Association Sportive Tanda|AS Tanda]] won their first league title, holding off [[ASEC Mimosas]] on the final day of the season. Entering with a one-point lead in the standings, [[Association Sportive Tanda|Tanda]] defeated [[CO Korhogo]] 2–1 at home to clinch the title even though [[ASEC Mimosas|ASEC]] got a 0–1 road win at [[Sporting Club de Gagnoa|Sporting Gagnoa]] to keep the pressure on. The league comprised 14 teams, the bottom two of which will be relegated to the 2016 [[Ligue 2 (Ivory Coast)|Ligue 2]]. Bouaké and [[Stella Club d'Adjamé|Stella]] each entered the final day of the season needing a win and to make up a large goal differential to avoid relegation, but both suffered road losses to seal their fate. ==Teams== A total of 14 teams will contest the league, including 12 sides from the [[2013–14 Ligue 1 (Ivory Coast)|2013–14 season]] and two promoted from the 2013–14 [[Ligue 2 (Ivory Coast)|Ligue 2]], [[Bouaké FC]] and [[Stade d'Abidjan]]. On the other hand, [[USC Bassam]] and [[CO Bouaflé]] were the last two teams of the [[2013–14 Ligue 1 (Ivory Coast)|2013–14 season]] and will play in [[Ligue 2 (Ivory Coast)|Ligue 2]] for the 2015 season.
